contradicting_evidence: Price-down/OI-down conditions and negative funding can support a rebound after positioning resets; they do not prove sustained selling will continue.
Extreme fear can accompany either continuing declines or exhaustion, limiting confidence in simple momentum extrapolation.
ETH's settled ETF flow was positive by $2.3 million, although that single observation does not confirm broader demand.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A downside-biased, uneven path is favored. Rebound attempts remain vulnerable to failed repair or renewed retests unless spot demand, ETH/BTC and participation improve together. Stabilization alone would weaken immediate momentum without confirming continuation upward.
falsification_conditions: BTC and ETH sustain recovery across repeated observations with improving executed spot demand, rather than a brief funding-driven squeeze.
Repeated breadth expansion and strengthening ETH/BTC accompany price resilience, undermining the failed-repair thesis.
missing_evidence: Repeated observations distinguishing temporary oversold conditions from durable demand.
Additional settled ETF sessions and refreshed supply-liquidity data.
Confirmation that breadth improvement, if observed, is persistent rather than a single same-family snapshot.
supporting_evidence: The selloff combines negative BTC/ETH price momentum, seller-dominated completed-hour flow and weakening ETH/BTC.

The earlier capitalization proxies show large- and mid-alt median daily losses near 8%, with very few advancers. These describe composition, not an independent breadth vote or canonical rotation signal.
Stablecoin supply declined approximately 1.53% over seven days and 5.41% over 30 days, providing a liquidity headwind without proving specific asset sales.
The latest settled BTC ETF session recorded $185.4 million of outflows, offering no confirmation of renewed institutional demand.
